WarMonitor RT @Anna_Giaritelli : An FAA employee who works at the national control center explained in a text message that shutting down the entire national airspace was "necessary" because "it snowballed quickly." "Those outage[s] did not just effect centers. There were towers and [Terminal Radar Approach Control facilities] with intermittent outages as well," the source said. "I absolutely understand why controllers are saying a nationwide ground stop was not needed. There were some areas that were not experiencing outages and the controllers working those areas wanted to keep traffic moving," the same employee said. "Facilities were losing their ability to speak to pilots in real time, and it snowballed quickly. The nationwide ground stop was 100% necessary for the safety of the flying public." tweet

Nuno Felix RT @DarkWebInformer : 🚨 🇪🇸 🇷🇺 Spanish police arrest suspected member of pro-Russian hacking group NoName057(16), seize arsenal of weapons and ammunition Spain's National Police have arrested a man in Burgos accused of establishing the country's first physical cell linked to NoName057(16), a pro-Russian hacktivist group blamed for at least 447 cyberattacks against Spanish government institutions, banks, and transportation companies since 2024. Authorities say the suspect was recruiting supporters, spreading propaganda, and encouraging cyberattacks against government institutions and violence against police officers. During searches, investigators seized semiautomatic firearms, shotguns, high-capacity magazines, more than 5,000 rounds of ammunition, chemicals, and three cryptocurrency hardware wallets containing Bitcoin. The suspect has been provisionally released under precautionary measures while investigations continue. The European Union sanctioned NoName057(16) on November 16. tweet
